prediction.likelyOutcome: Dover Mall is very likely to prevail on liability and on the accuracy of its stated damages of $276,089.72, with the COVID-based frustration/impossibility defenses unlikely to survive given the lease's explicit force majeure rent carve-out. The mitigation defense is the genuine wildcard — Dover Mall's admitted lack of evidence of reletting efforts creates real (though unquantified on this record) risk of a partial reduction or a trial-worthy fact issue on damages, so full recovery of the requested amount is likely but not assured.

outcome.description: The Superior Court granted the landlord summary judgment on liability and damages in the amount of $276,089.72, the full amount demanded, holding the force majeure clause allocated pandemic-closure risk to the tenant and two lease provisions relieved the landlord of any duty to relet. No attorney's fee award is stated. This is a trial-level decision; no appeal is reflected in the opinion.
outcome.appellateChange: n/a (trial-level decision; no appeal in opinion)
